narrative.title: The Supply Chain Order Assembler
narrative.scenario: A fulfillment scanner reads one long stream of crate codes and must locate the shortest contiguous stretch that contains every part code on today's pick list — counting multiplicity, so a part demanded twice must appear twice. The scanner slides a frame over the stream, records the first complete covering stretch, then keeps tightening from the left as long as coverage holds, tracking the shortest frame ever seen.
narrative.inputFormat: Two strings: s (the crate-code stream) and t (the pick list).
narrative.outputFormat: Return the shortest substring of s covering every character of t with multiplicity, or an empty string if none exists.
constraints: s and t consist of uppercase and lowercase English letters
The answer is guaranteed to be unique when it exists

testCases.explanation: The tail "BANC" is the shortest stretch holding A, B and C simultaneously.
The single character covers the demand exactly.

hintLevels: Level 1: Track how many distinct letters still lack their full quota — coverage is binary per letter.
Level 2: Expand until every letter's deficit hits zero, then shrink from the left while coverage holds.
Level 3: Record the window right before each shrink; the map can go negative for surplus letters, which is fine.
